quizName: DMV Practice Test #15 25 Questions • Passing Score 20

questions.question: If you have a passenger on your motorcycle, you should do all of the following, except:

options.text: Ride slower than usual.
Allow more distance to stop than usual.
Tell the passenger to hold onto the back of the bike.

questions.correctAnswerText: Tell the passenger to hold onto the back of the bike.
questions.explanation: A motorcycle with a passenger handles differently because of the extra weight. Ride slower and allow more time and distance to stop. The passenger should hold firmly onto the passenger handgrips or onto your waist, hips, or midsection.

questions.question: If you need to react to a hazard on the road, do not:

options.text: Avoid communicating with other drivers.
Adjust your speed accordingly.
Make your presence known by sounding your horn or using lights or signals.

questions.correctAnswerText: Avoid communicating with other drivers.
questions.explanation: To stay safe, communicate with other drivers by using your horn, lights, and signals. Adjust your speed for the situation. Change your lane position or direction if needed.

questions.question: When parked on the road, a motorcycle should:

options.text: Create an angle with the curb between 45 and 90 degrees.
Be parked without a wheel or fender touching the curb.
Be parked parallel to the curb.

questions.correctAnswerText: Create an angle with the curb between 45 and 90 degrees.
questions.explanation: When parked on the road, a motorcycle should create an angle with the curb between 45 and 90 degrees. A wheel or fender should touch the curb.

questions.question: To swerve correctly, you should:

options.text: Shift your weight quickly.
Turn the handlebars quickly.
Press the handgrip in the direction of the turn.

questions.correctAnswerText: Press the handgrip in the direction of the turn.
questions.explanation: To swerve away from a hazard, press lightly on the handgrip on the side where you want to go.

questions.question: When passing a vehicle, you:

options.text: May exceed the speed limit by 10 mph.
Must not exceed the speed limit.
Are required to ride faster than the speed limit.

questions.correctAnswerText: Must not exceed the speed limit.
questions.explanation: You must stay within the speed limit when passing. Only pass another vehicle where it is safe and legal.

questions.question: What does a solid red arrow on a traffic signal mean?

options.text: Drivers must come to a complete stop.
Drivers may proceed through the intersection with caution.
Drivers must yield to oncoming traffic.

questions.correctAnswerText: Drivers must come to a complete stop.
questions.explanation: A solid red arrow means the same as a red light. Stop completely and wait for a signal that lets you turn in the direction you want to go.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?

options.text: Signal ahead
Crossroad ahead
Divided roadway ahead

questions.correctAnswerText: Divided roadway ahead
questions.explanation: Warning signs are yellow with black letters or symbols. They tell drivers about road conditions ahead. This sign warns you that the road will be divided.

questions.question: When it starts raining, it is best to:

options.text: Get off the road.
Ride in the tire tracks left by other vehicles.
Ride in the center portion of the lane.

questions.correctAnswerText: Ride in the tire tracks left by other vehicles.
questions.explanation: When it rains, do not ride in the center of the lane. Instead, ride in the tire tracks left by cars ahead of you. The left tire track is often the best choice, but this can change based on traffic.

questions.question: When preparing to ride with a passenger, instruct the passenger to:

options.text: Get on the motorcycle before you.
Sit as far back as possible.
Hold firmly onto your waist, hips, or belt.

questions.correctAnswerText: Hold firmly onto your waist, hips, or belt.
questions.explanation: Ask your passenger to wait until after you start the engine before getting on. They should sit as far forward as possible without crowding you and hold firmly onto your waist, hips, or belt.

questions.question: When riding in a group, a distance of _____ should be maintained between the lead rider and the rider directly behind them.

options.text: One second
Two seconds
Three seconds

questions.correctAnswerText: Three seconds
questions.explanation: When riding in a staggered group under normal conditions, each rider should keep a normal three-second distance from the rider ahead.

questions.question: When riding over scored pavement in a work zone, what should you do?

options.text: Look down to see the road surface changes.
Keep your head and eyes up.
Stay on the left side of the lane.

questions.correctAnswerText: Keep your head and eyes up.
questions.explanation: Keep your head and eyes up when riding over scored pavement in a work zone. Ride slowly and keep a steady throttle. Do not fight the handlebars.

questions.question: Before you start riding, the fuel valve should be:

options.text: Open.
Closed.
Covered.

questions.correctAnswerText: Open.
questions.explanation: Make sure your fuel valve is open before you ride. If the valve is closed, the engine may start using fuel left in the lines from before. But it will stop running once those lines are empty.

questions.question: Your lane position should do all of the following, except:

options.text: Give you an escape route.
Help you experience wind blasts.
Show other drivers your intentions.

questions.correctAnswerText: Help you experience wind blasts.
questions.explanation: Good lane position helps you see others and be seen. It helps you avoid wind blasts, blind spots, and road hazards. Your position should discourage other riders from sharing your lane and give you a way to escape if danger appears.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?

options.text: No right turn
No left turn
No U-turn

questions.correctAnswerText: No U-turn
questions.explanation: Regulatory signs are white with red and black markings. They tell drivers about traffic laws in that area. This sign means U-turns are not allowed.

questions.question: A front wheel and handlebar wobble is usually caused by:

options.text: Wrong tire pressure or uneven weight.
Front wheel not tightened properly to the frame.
Hitting something with the front tire.

questions.correctAnswerText: Wrong tire pressure or uneven weight.
questions.explanation: A wobble is when the front wheel and handlebars shake side to side. Most wobbles come from improper weight distribution, wrong accessories, or incorrect tire pressure.

questions.question: Your normal scanning routine while riding should include:

options.text: Always looking in the rearview mirror.
Checking the rearview mirror often.
Never using the rearview mirror.

questions.correctAnswerText: Checking the rearview mirror often.
questions.explanation: Check your mirrors often as part of your normal scanning. Also check your mirrors before changing lanes, at intersections, and before slowing down.

questions.question: Why is it dangerous for a motorcyclist to ride next to another vehicle?

options.text: The other vehicle may block your escape route.
Other drivers can easily see you.
You cannot read road signs.

questions.correctAnswerText: The other vehicle may block your escape route.
questions.explanation: Riding next to another vehicle is unsafe because the vehicle could move into your lane and hit you. It could also block your escape route if a hazard appears.

questions.question: If a dog is chasing you, you should:

options.text: Stop your motorcycle until the dog loses interest.
Slow down as you approach the dog, then speed up quickly as it gets close.
Swerve around the dog.

questions.correctAnswerText: Slow down as you approach the dog, then speed up quickly as it gets close.
questions.explanation: When you see a dog approaching, slow down and downshift until you are near the dog. Then speed up quickly as the dog gets close.

questions.question: If you cannot avoid an obstacle on the road, you should:

options.text: Speed up before hitting the object.
Stay seated so the seat absorbs the impact.
Hit the obstacle at a 90-degree angle if possible.

questions.correctAnswerText: Hit the obstacle at a 90-degree angle if possible.
questions.explanation: If you cannot avoid an obstacle, slow down. Try to hit it at as close to a 90-degree angle as possible.

questions.question: When taking a curve in a group, riders should be in:

options.text: A single-file line.
Pairs.
A staggered line.

questions.correctAnswerText: A single-file line.
questions.explanation: Groups usually ride in a staggered line. Move to a single-file line when taking a curve, making a turn, entering a highway, or leaving a highway.

questions.question: When passing another vehicle, what should you do?

options.text: You can go faster than the speed limit until you finish passing.
You can ignore no-passing zone markings if you started the pass in a passing zone.
You must follow the posted speed limit.

questions.correctAnswerText: You must follow the posted speed limit.
questions.explanation: Always stay within the speed limit when passing. Only pass in areas where passing is allowed.

questions.question: What is one difference between goggles and a windshield?

options.text: Goggles protect your eyes from wind, but a windshield does not.
A windshield protects your eyes from wind, but goggles do not.
A windshield keeps your eyes from watering better than goggles.

questions.correctAnswerText: Goggles protect your eyes from wind, but a windshield does not.
questions.explanation: Goggles protect your eyes from wind. A windshield does not provide this protection. A windshield is not a substitute for goggles or a face shield.

questions.question: What does a flashing red traffic light mean?

options.text: Stop completely, then go when it is safe.
Only stop if you need to yield to other traffic.
Other vehicles are entering the roadway.

questions.correctAnswerText: Stop completely, then go when it is safe.
questions.explanation: A flashing red light means the same as a stop sign. Come to a complete stop. Let all crossing traffic and pedestrians pass. Then go when it is safe.

questions.question: Is it good to use all three lane positions?

options.text: No, because you will not get used to any part of the lane.
No, because it confuses other drivers.
Yes, when road and traffic conditions change.

questions.correctAnswerText: Yes, when road and traffic conditions change.
questions.explanation: No single lane position is always best. Change your position as road and traffic conditions change.

questions.question: When turning, what should you do?

options.text: Move your knees away from the gas tank.
Turn only your head to look through the turn, not your shoulders.
Turn your head and shoulders to look through the turn.

questions.correctAnswerText: Turn only your head to look through the turn, not your shoulders.
questions.explanation: When turning, look toward where you want to go. Turn only your head and keep your eyes level. Do not turn your shoulders, as this can cause you to steer off course.
